start.label: from about October 1892 (the acquaintance's documented start)

summary: Sidney Mavor was one of the young men of Alfred Taylor's Little College Street household; the trial record documents nights spent there in Taylor's company, and nothing more specific between the two of them.

disputed.claim: That the shared nights at Little College Street were sexual.
disputed.asserted_by: The prosecution's framing of Taylor's rooms and the shared-bed testimony at the 1895 proceedings
disputed.disputed_by: No witness attests a sexual act between Mavor and Taylor; Mavor denied on oath that any impropriety ever took place (in the Wilde context) and the Mavor counts were struck
disputed.grounds: Shared-bed and household evidence only; the act-level testimony at Taylor's rooms concerns other parties.

sources.quote: Were Taylor's visitors, as a class, women or men?—Men—young men from sixteen to thirty. … Others were Sidney Ma[v]or, Charles Mason, and Ernest Macklin. Mavor and Mason stayed there for nights with Taylor.
sources.context: Testimony of Ellen Grant, landlady of 13 Little College Street, Regina v. Wilde and Taylor, April-May 1895
sources.supports: The household pattern and Mavor's nights at Taylor's, from the landlady.
sources.provenance: IA in.ernet.dli.2015.499238, printed p. 199 read as IIIF page image.
sources.speaker: Ellen Grant, landlady of 13 Little College Street
